Anterior segment evaluation revealed diffusely congested conjunctiva and multiple nummular infiltrates with positive fluorescein staining concentrated over the central cornea in the right eye. The left eye showed minimal conjunctival congestion and nummular infiltrates with a cataractous lens (nuclear sclerosis grade II), as shown in Figure 1.

in_text_mentions: The patient was started on moxifloxacin 0.5% eye drops eight times a day along with adequate lubricating eye drops. He was followed up closely, and at the third-day review, vision had dropped to 6/12 in the right eye and 6/18 in the left eye. Anterior segment examination showed diffuse superficial punctate keratitis with positive fluorescein staining in both eyes, which progressed to SEIs with negative fluorescein staining over the next five days, predominantly affecting the central cornea, as seen in Figure 3.

in_text_mentions: 43 photographs of the MSI were collected and analyzed (Fig. 1). There was significant difference among 3 regions of cornea, in terms of the probability of each region involved by MSI (P = 0.000, Fisher’s exact test). The probability of central region involvement was significantly higher than that of pericentral region involvement (P = 0.015, Fisher’s exact test) and peripheral region involvement (P = 0.000, Fisher’s exact test) (Table 5). in_text_mentions: A husband and wife presented with a history of redness in both eyes for 10 days and blurred vision and photophobia for three days. On examination, the wife had conjunctival congestion and a few SEIs in the pupillary area, with vision of 6/12 in both eyes. The husband had a few SEIs with vision of 6/9 in both eyes. Both were treated with topical loteprednol five times a day. After six weeks, they improved significantly, achieving 6/6 vision in both eyes with complete resolution of nummular lesions, as shown in Figure 6.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows fluorescein-stained punctate epithelial keratitis in a patient with adenoviral epidemic keratoconjunctivitis. B: Panel B is in vivo confocal microscopy of an EKC patient showing basal epithelial cell clusters and inflammatory infiltration, findings not in the provided vocabulary. C: Panel C shows increased Langerhans cells on confocal microscopy in EKC, a captioned disease-associated finding absent from the vocabulary. D: Panel D shows anterior stromal hyperreflectivity on confocal microscopy in EKC, a captioned finding not represented in the vocabulary.

in_text_mentions: Clinical EKC eyes evaluated during the punctate epithelial keratitis stage showed cell clusters surrounded by inflammatory cell infiltration in the basal epithelium. An increased number of branching dendritic cells were observed in Bowman’s layer. Hyperreflective cells were noted in the anterior stroma (Figure 2).

plate_findings.evidence: Areas of subepithelial infiltration (A); in-text: subepithelial infiltrate period

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Corneal image labeled as showing areas of subepithelial infiltration during EKC, a classic EKC corneal manifestation. B: Confocal corneal image from an EKC patient showing a focus of hyperreflective keratitis in the basal epithelium; finding is not fully captured by the provided vocabulary. C: Confocal image from an EKC patient showing subbasal Langerhans cell connections; this is an inflammatory corneal imaging finding but is nonspecific and absent from the vocabulary. D: Confocal corneal image showing a round anterior stromal hyperreflective plaque during EKC, consistent with subepithelial corneal infiltrates.
panels.attribution_text: Subaşı et al. In Vivo Confocal Microscopy Analysis of the Corneal Layers in Adenoviral Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis. Turkish journal of ophthalmology 2018. doi:10.4274/tjo.59251. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Areas of subepithelial infiltration (A); focus of hyperreflective keratitis in the basal epithelium (B); Langerhans cell connections in the subbasal plexus (C); and focal hyperreflective plaque with round border in the anterior stroma (arrow) (D)
in_text_mentions: In the subepithelial infiltrate period, the basal epithelium still exhibited hyperreflective foci and inflammatory cells, but the areas of anterior stromal hyperreflectivity formed more distinct round hyperreflective plaques. The eyes exhibited no changes in the deep stromal layers or endothelium during the course of EKC (Figure 4).
